Diego (Eng): Hey team—my 2026 W-2 just posted and shows NH state withholding only. I moved to NY on 2026-07-10 and updated my address same day. I thought NY withholding should apply for the latter half of the year. How does this get fixed?
Lina (People Ops): Sorry for the hassle, Diego. Can you confirm the date you updated your address in Ripley and whether you completed NY payroll enrollment?
Diego (Eng): Updated profile 2026-07-10 08:15 ET. I filled the enrollment form but didn't get a confirmation email.
Sam (Payroll): Thanks. If the NY enrollment wasn't active before the payroll cutoff, the system would have kept NH withholding. We can either: 1) issue a corrective W-2c if withholding was wrong, or 2) process a payroll adjustment to withhold NY for paid period retroactively and then file amended returns. Need to check whether NY residency rules apply from 7/10.
Alicia (Tax Counsel): High-level: state taxing rights vary—NY has part-year resident rules. If Diego became NY resident on 7/10, income earned after that date is NY taxable. We can correct with amended state filings and a W-2c. That usually resolves withholding mismatches.
